title: Security posture discovery - Sapphire Financial
summary: High-level security discovery covering SOC 2 / ISO readiness, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC model, audit logs and SIEM integration, KMS/BYOK options, and data retention/deletion. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads; requested SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs, and sample SAML metadata. Agreed next step: send security pack, schedule technical deep dive for infra team and run a short pilot/benchmark.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 16:30 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Marcus Li (CISO, Sapphire Financial), Dana Ortiz (Head of Platform), Evan Patel (Staff SRE)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Security posture discovery focused on certifications, identity, encryption, logs, and data retention. Customer evaluating Dedicated or Private for regulated workloads.

00:00 Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we got about 55 minutes on the calendar, thanks for taking time. i'm alex chen, i'm the AE on this account; jordan park from our infra team is with me, he'll handle the technical bits.
00:18 Marcus Li: thanks alex. yeah, hi all, i'm marcus, ciso at sapphire. dana and evan from platform and sre are here too. we wanted to run through your security posture, certs, and how identity and keys are handled so we can decide hosted vs dedicated.
00:35 Jordan Park: yeah great, i'll jump in on technical. just to set expectations, we can cover SOC2/ISO, sso/saml, rbac, audit logs, kms, retention. feel free to interrupt, and we can follow up with deeper calls.
00:50 Dana Ortiz: quick one — our default preference is private in VPC, but we want to understand delta if we did Redwood hosted with dedicated capacity. cost and network egress aside — security is the gating criteria.
01:06 Alex Chen: totally fair. many customers start on hosted for speed, but you can move to dedicated or private — and we have clear controls around data isolation. for regulated data most customers do dedicated or private.
01:20 Marcus Li: can you confirm your SOC and ISO posture? we need SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence for our procurement.
01:30 Jordan Park: yes — we are SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. i'll send the report and scope after this call. side note, sometimes the transcription of product names is funky — we call our offering Redwood Hosted, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private.
01:46 Evan Patel: and are the reports redacted or full? we need details on control mappings and the subservice providers.
01:55 Alex Chen: we typically provide SOC2 Type II attestation and ISO certificate under NDA; the SOC report includes control mappings and lists subservice providers — we can provide a redacted copy initially and full under NDA.
02:10 Marcus Li: good. identity — we use Okta as our primary IdP and SCIM for user provisioning. we need SAML SSO, SCIM group sync, and support for role mapping into your RBAC.
02:25 Jordan Park: we support SAML 2.0 IdP integrations and SCIM for provisioning. for RBAC we have built-in roles (admin, dev, observer) and you can map SAML attributes to roles. we also support custom role definitions for dedicated/private deployments.
02:45 Dana Ortiz: is role enforcement at the control plane only or do you have per-route token permissions on the data plane?
02:55 Jordan Park: good question — we enforce at the control plane for console/API operations. for data plane access (model inference), we have token-level scoping; on exclusive Dedicated/Private you can enforce network level controls and mTLS between services. some smaller customers on Hosted use API keys + scoped routes.
03:22 Marcus Li: audit logs — we need immutable logs, long-term retention (at least 1 year), and streaming to our SIEM (Splunk). do you push logs or do we pull?
03:35 Alex Chen: we provide audit logs from the control plane that include user actions and API calls. for Dedicated/Private customers we can set up log forwarding to your SIEM (Splunk/Kafka/S3) and we support syslog/HTTPS endpoints. retention is configurable; default hosted retention is shorter but Dedicated/Private can be set to 365 days or more.
03:58 Evan Patel: what about request/response logging — will inference payloads be included in logs? we need to avoid PII being stored in logs.
04:10 Jordan Park: by default we log metadata (request id, model, tokens, latency) but not full user prompts/output unless you enable full logging for debugging. we also provide automatic PII redaction options and support data masking. for compliance-heavy customers we recommend disabling full payload logging and using sample traces with redaction.
04:36 Marcus Li: encryption at rest and in transit — what's your KMS model? BYOK? HSM?
04:44 Jordan Park: we encrypt in transit with TLS, in rest we use cloud KMS. for Hosted customers we manage keys by default; for Dedicated we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS and for Private deployments you can integrate your HSM or KMS. we also support envelope encryption.
05:05 Dana Ortiz: do you support bring-your-own-key with key rotation policies and separation of control plane access? we need proof that even Redwood operators can't read data.
05:20 Jordan Park: for BYOK the keys live in your KMS and Redwood uses them for encryption operations; we offer limited key usage patterns so that plaintext never lands on Redwood-managed persistent storage. for Private deployments of course you control everything on-prem. we can provide architecture diagrams.
05:38 Marcus Li: operator access — can you describe privileged access and how it's logged?
05:44 Alex Chen: we have role-based admin controls for Redwood staff, emergency access is tightly controlled via approved jump boxes, and everything is logged in our audit system. access requests are w/ justifications, and we can share our access control policy in the security pack.
06:05 Evan Patel: do you have cross-tenant isolation guarantees? for Dedicated is there a shared control plane with isolation at the data plane?
06:18 Jordan Park: Dedicated keeps customer inference workloads in reserved GPU pools; control plane is multi-tenant but logically separated and access-controlled. for Private deployments you get a separate control plane in your VPC if requested. we can provide details on network segmentation and tenancy model in the technical deep dive.
06:40 Marcus Li: data residency — we need data to stay in us-east-1 for regulatory reasons. how do you guarantee region pinning?
06:48 Jordan Park: we support region pinning for data and inference. for Hosted we have region options and can pin requests to US regions. Dedicated and Private are easier to guarantee. we'll note region configuration in the pilot scope.
07:03 Dana Ortiz: incident response — do you have an incident timeline and notify customers within X hours?
07:10 Alex Chen: yes, we have an incident response policy; for major incidents we notify customers within 1 hour and provide postmortems. we can share our incident SLA and playbooks in the pack.
07:25 Marcus Li: what about pen tests and third-party assessments?
07:30 Jordan Park: we do annual pentests and vulnerability scans; scope and report summaries are included in SOC2/ISO materials. for Dedicated/Private customers we can arrange targeted assessments under NDA.
07:45 Evan Patel: regulatory — any PCI/hipaa specifics? we are not PCI but we do have some healthcare PII in certain datasets — will that constrain hosted?
07:58 Alex Chen: we support HIPAA workflows on Dedicated/Private with BAAs; Hosted can be used but typically customers needing full HIPAA controls choose Dedicated or Private.
08:12 Marcus Li: can you walk through a typical RBAC mapping? like, how would Okta groups map to roles and what granularity do we get?
08:22 Jordan Park: typical pattern: Okta groups sync via SCIM to Redwood groups; SAML attributes map to role claims at login. roles can be organization-wide or project-scoped; you can create custom permissions on a per-route basis — e.g., allow inference:submit but deny model:deploy. on Dedicated you can also enforce network ACLs per project.
09:01 Dana Ortiz: do you have separation between metadata and content so that metadata (like audit logs) doesn't contain prompts?
09:10 Jordan Park: yes metadata is stored separately; logs are designed to be metadata-first unless full payload logging is explicitly enabled. we log request ids and token counts; payloads are opt-in.
09:30 Marcus Li: record retention and deletion — we need to support deletion requests and have SLA for deletes, plus proof that backups are scrubbed.
09:45 Jordan Park: for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention windows — we support immediate deletion requests with background scrub; backups are rotated and we can provide retention policies. for Hosted default retention is shorter but deletions are honored; we'll provide the delete flow and timelines in writing.
10:12 Evan Patel: curious about KV cache/ prefix caching — do you ever surface cached content in logs or to other tenants?
10:20 Jordan Park: caching is isolated per customer; KV cache is scoped to model sessions within a tenant and not shared cross-tenant. we avoid surfacing cached prompts in cluster-level debugging logs.
10:40 Marcus Li: okay, governance stuff — can we get an SOC2 mapping to our control framework?
10:46 Alex Chen: yes, we'll provide a control mapping document that maps Redwood controls to your framework; that's part of the security pack.
11:00 Dana Ortiz: for SAML metadata, is there a standard SAML cert rotation flow? we rotate certs quarterly.
11:09 Jordan Park: we support SAML cert rotation — you can upload new certs and we have a window for rotation without downtime. we'll include SAML metadata examples.
11:25 Marcus Li: any third-party subprocessors we should know about? cloud providers, monitoring vendors, etc.
11:32 Alex Chen: primary subservice providers are public cloud vendors (AWS/GCP), CDN and monitoring tools; we'll list them in SOC2 and the subservice provider list.
11:45 Evan Patel: do you offer dedicated logging endpoints so we keep logs in our own S3?
11:50 Jordan Park: yes we can forward logs to your S3 bucket or push to your Splunk HTTP collector; for Dedicated we can do direct aggregation into your Kinesis or Kafka.
12:03 Marcus Li: about operator access again — can we get a read-only view of operator sessions? we want to audit if any manual ops occur.
12:13 Alex Chen: operator actions are logged, and we can provide audit trail exports; if there's a need for realtime session streaming we can discuss an integration.
12:30 Dana Ortiz: one more — encryption key rotation cadence and how that impacts running inferences.
12:38 Jordan Park: key rotation is supported; for envelope encryption your workloads continue during rotation. for BYOK we rely on your KMS rotation policies; we can coordinate to minimize impact.
13:00 Marcus Li: what about long-term retention of training-derived artifacts? we aren't doing training on your platform but want to ensure outputs aren't used for model training.
13:12 Alex Chen: we do not use customer inference payloads for model training unless you opt in; that's a policy we can include in the contract.
13:28 Evan Patel: can you talk about physical security and datacenter certifications?
13:34 Jordan Park: we inherit cloud providers' physical security and certifications; we can provide certs for data centers via the cloud provider statements and include those references.
13:50 Marcus Li: okay, for next steps we need the SOC2 + ISO docs, a technical deep dive w/ infra, and sample SAML metadata. also want to scope a 2-week Dedicated pilot to run small traffic and latency tests.
14:10 Alex Chen: understood. jordan will scope the benchmark and we'll send the security pack. any questions about pricing or timelines?
14:20 Dana Ortiz: pricing — dedicated pricing must include support for 24/7 access for incidents. is that an add-on?
14:28 Alex Chen: yes enterprise support and on-call SLAs are an add-on; we'll include options in the follow-up.
14:40 Marcus Li: final compliance question — do you support customer-managed purging of telemetry across all logs, including backups?
14:50 Jordan Park: we can provide purge workflows and proof of deletion for Dedicated/Private; hosted is possible but backup scrub timelines vary. we'll document the exact timelines and procedures.
15:10 Evan Patel: any gotchas we should know before we start the pilot? network egress, model licensing, seq length limits?
15:22 Jordan Park: model licensing is handled per model; sequence length and GPU type will affect latency/cost. network egress and region pinning are aspects we'll clarify in the pilot scope.
15:40 Marcus Li: ok thank you — let's get the docs, we'll review with our compliance team.
15:46 Alex Chen: thanks all. we will: send SOC2 + ISO, security questionnaire, sample SAML metadata, and draft pilot plan. jordan will reach out to schedule the deep dive.
15:58 Dana Ortiz: thanks everyone.
16:02 Meeting end / recorder stopped.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (product names, small punctuation errors) and filler language. follow-ups are explicit in next_steps and action_items above.
